title: Lotuswell Clinic — inference intake notes
content:
Meeting / context
- 2024-11-02 initial intake call with Lotuswell Clinic (regional outpatient chain, ~12 sites). Goal: evaluate private-deploy option for a clinician triage assistant that summarizes intake and suggests next steps. Primary drivers: PHI protection, low-latency in-clinic UX, predictable monthly cost.

Participants
- Lotuswell: Dr. Mina Patel (CMO), Ravi Shah (IT ops), Elena Gutiérrez (telehealth lead)
- Redwood: Anika (solutions), Leo (privacy/security), Priya (platform integration)

Top-level asks from Lotuswell
1) Private deployment (VPC) with no egress to public internet for model inference; control plane acceptable to remain hosted if secured.
2) Support HL7 FHIR canonicalization for intake records; map to prompts/templates.
3) Latency SLO: median response <400ms for 64-token summary for in-clinic tablet UX. 95th <800ms.
4) Throughput: steady 12 concurrent sessions during peak, spikes to 40 concurrent; estimate ~1000 requests/day.
5) Strong audit logs / tamper-evident retention for 90 days.
6) Model behavior constraints: conservative hallucination profile; high precision for medication/diagnosis extraction.
7) Data residency: primary region us-east-1; option for EU region for certain sites.

Priority requirements (MVP)
- Technical
  - Private deployment (VPC peering or private-link) + optional on-prem inference bundle if needed.
  - KMS integration for keys (Vault / AWS KMS). Customer prefers KMS with HSM-backed keys for signing logs.
  - FHIR -> prompt translation layer: deterministic templates + extraction post-processors.
  - Rate limiter at gateway to protect latency SLOs and avoid noisy neighbors.
- Security / compliance
  - PHI never leaves VPC; no third-party logging unless explicitly permitted.
  - Audit trail of prompts/responses hashed+signed daily for tamper evidence.
  - SOC2 & HIPAA BAA conversation necessary (ask legal).
- Ops
  - Canary rollout to 2 pilot clinics, then roll to all 12.
  - Cost visibility on per-site basis in Redwood Console.

Suggested architecture (text sketch)
- Lotuswell EHR -> Transform service (in their infra) -> Private API endpoint in redwood private deployment (VPC peering) -> Redwood runtime (pinned model variant for safety) -> Post-processing service (entity extraction, FHIR backfill) -> EHR.
- Optional: run the transform + post-processing inside customer network (preferred) and only send compact prompt to Redwood.

Model / inference notes
- Recommend starting with a smaller safe-guarded model variant (quantized) for summaries to meet latency/cost targets; keep a higher-capacity model in Dedicated pool for complex cases.
- Use prefix caching for standard intake templates to reduce tokens and latency.
- Configure maximum output tokens to 80 for summaries; use token budget enforcement in the gateway.

Latency / capacity planning
- 12 steady concurrent sessions -> target reserved capacity of 2 x A10-style GPU (TBD) or equivalent in Redwood Dedicated for predictable P99s. (We need infra team to translate to instance types.)
- Need to measure cold-start of KV cache for first request of a patient session; expected additional 50-120ms.

Cost expectations (rough)
- MVP monthly: private infra + reserved capacity + support = rough estimate $18k–$30k/mo depending on instance choices and audit retention. (Need finance quote.)

Security & compliance checklist (customer asks)
- BAA signature required; provide HIPAA-specific dataflow diagram.
- KMS/HSM integration and key rotation policy.
- SIEM integration: send audit metadata to customer Splunk via whitelist (no raw PHI).
- Pen test window and agreed scope prior to pilot.

Prompting / evaluation guidance
- Avoid free-form hallucination: include instruction block in prompt template that requires model to return structured JSON with provenance flags and confidence score.
- Example prompt template (MVP):
  "You are a clinical summarizer. Take the following intake notes and return: (1) concise problem list (short bullets), (2) red flags (list), (3) recommended disposition (0: self-care, 1: schedule urgent visit, 2: refer specialist) and (4) confidence 0–1 with justification. Use only information in the intake. If unsure, say 'insufficient data'."
- Post-processing: verify extracted medications against formulary; query small clinical knowledge database locally to reduce hallucination risk.

Edge cases and gotchas (observed in other pilots)
- Long structured intake -> token bloat. Mitigation: move heavy structured data as compressed keys or only send diffs.
- Clinician edits required -> must audit both original and edited outputs and store diffs.
- EHR mapping mismatches (free-text vs coded fields). Build mapping table and a fallback manual review queue.
- Rate limiting from clinic NAT gateways can add unpredictable latency; coordinate with Lotuswell network team.
- PHI in logs: default Redwood Console traces may include tokens; ensure console masking or disable token-level traces for this deployment.

Monitoring & quality
- Define launched prompt set (~200 prompts) and expected golden outputs for regression testing. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization/batching settings after we feed usage distribution.
- Key metrics: precision/recall for med extraction, summary brevity (tokens), median latency, confidence calibration.

Rollout plan (phases)
- Phase 0 (prework, 2 weeks): legal (BAA), network prep (VPC info), shortlist EHR endpoints and sample data sandbox (anonymized). Assign: Ravi (Lotuswell) to share network CIDRs by 2024-11-10.
- Phase 1 (pilot, 4 weeks): deploy private instance in us-east-1, connect 2 pilot clinics, test latency and accuracy. Assign: Redwood infra (Priya) + Leo for KMS config.
- Phase 2 (expanded pilot, 6 weeks): add post-processing for medication checks, integrate audit pipeline to customer SIEM.
- Phase 3 (production): roll to 12 sites, enable cost reporting per site.

Open questions (for next call)
- Does Lotuswell require on-prem inference (air-gapped) for any single site? (Dr. Patel hinted maybe one site).
- Which EHR vendor versions do we need to support? Need sample FHIR bundles and mapping table.
- Legal: exact BAA clauses around logging retention and signed hashes.
- Network ops: preferred connectivity method (VPC peering vs PrivateLink) and allowed ports.
- SLA expectations (uptime/response) — they asked about 99.9% initially but need to confirm P99 latency objective.

Immediate next steps (owners + dates)
- Send intake summary + architecture sketch to Lotuswell (Anika) — due 2024-11-04.
- Redwood infra to produce preliminary instance/cost options for private deploy (Priya) — due 2024-11-08.
- Security to draft BAA checklist + list of required audits (Leo) — due 2024-11-07.
- Lotuswell (Ravi) to provide sample anonymized FHIR bundles and network CIDRs — due 2024-11-10.
- Create JIRA epic and link Confluence page (Anika) — done: JIRA:CS-4821, confluence:LOTUSWELL-TRIAGE-PROTOTYPE.

Notes to self / things to remember
- Offer a fallback policy: if production latency spikes, route to a smaller model variant or return a brief templated message.
- Keep patient-facing language conservative; have clinical reviewer for any automation that suggests disposition.
- Add an early eval of hallucination rate on meds extraction with synthetic tests.

Meeting cadence suggestion
- Weekly 30m sync during pilot (Mon 11am PT) + weekly async status in shared channel.

End of notes.
